headline: Trump is reportedly ignoring an alleged Nvidia espionage plot as a lawmaker threatens hearings, Pope Leo XIV called for the 'disarmament' of AI, and reports described burnout among humans fighting the fallout from 'Black October's' AI-enabled cyberattacks.

points.text: A newsletter roundup reported that Trump is ignoring an alleged Nvidia espionage plot, as Rep. Casar threatens hearings over the matter.
Pope Leo XIV called for the 'disarmament' of AI, saying machines are tools, not persons, and that humans have the responsibility to guide, change and, when necessary, reject its applications.

Axios reported that the humans on the frontlines of AI-enabled cyberattacks are burning out under a barrage of attacks, vulnerabilities and false alarms following this month's 'Black October' vulnerability disclosures.
A newsletter reflected on whether it had been wrong about open models and cyber risk, noting that 'Black October' marked the moment AI-model-driven cyber risks began to materialize.
Wired's Uncanny Valley podcast discussed how a contractor's personal Claude agent got into a secure Pentagon network, alongside Anthropic's IPO filing.
The ITU's AI for Good initiative highlighted Zhejiang Lab's '021' scientific foundation model, built to work across many sciences.
